source:
I want to build a 3D racing game where the player controls a dragon flying through a sequence of rings to complete a course.

Here are the core requirements for the game:
1. Player Controller:
 • The player controls a 3D dragon character.
 • Flight controls should include pitch (up/down), yaw (left/right), and roll.
 • Include a forward thrust/speed mechanic, and gravity that pulls the dragon down slightly if they aren't actively flying.
2. Camera System:
 • Implement a third-person follow camera that stays behind and slightly above the dragon, smoothly rotating as the dragon turns.
3. Course & Ring Mechanics:
 • Create a system for placing floating rings in the environment.
 • The player must fly through the rings in a specific, numbered order.
 • When the player passes through the correct active ring, play a sound, change the ring's color (e.g., from yellow to green), and activate the next ring in the sequence.
4. Win/Loss State & UI:
 • Include a simple HUD (Heads Up Display) showing a countdown timer and a ring counter (e.g., "Rings: 3/10").
 • Win State: Passing through the final ring before time runs out.
 • Loss State: The timer hitting zero before the course is finished, or crashing into the ground/terrain.

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the world below read as high fantasy, or something else?
answers.answer: Use a simple high-fantasy environment below the course, fitting the dragon flight premise.

answers.ask: How many rings should the course have? The HUD example implies ten.
answers.answer: Use 10 rings, as implied by the HUD example.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No theme was stated - should the world below read as high fantasy, or something else? A: Use a simple high-fantasy environment below the course, fitting the dragon flight premise.
- [author] ring count — Q: How many rings should the course have? The HUD example implies ten. A: Use 10 rings, as implied by the HUD example.
- [agent_inferred] course ending — Q: Is this a point-to-point course or a loop? A: It is point-to-point, ending at the tenth ring.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a 3D high-fantasy dragon flight course made from exactly 10 large floating rings arranged in a clearly numbered point-to-point sequence through open air. Begin with a visible starting marker just before ring 1 and make ring 10 a distinct finish gate. Space and orient the rings to create a smooth forward aerial route with room for pitch, yaw, and roll, while keeping the sequence visually traceable and avoiding ambiguous crossings. Place a simple high-fantasy landscape below the course as the ground hazard and backdrop, framing the entire ring chain in one elevated aerial view.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Racing (`racing`), specifically a finite aerial ring race.

## Shape and preset
Use `route-point-to-point`: the course starts before ring 1 and ends at ring 10. Use the Sprint / Drag preset for its defined start and terminal finish, dropping `lane-corridor` because the ordered floating rings define an open-air route rather than a divided surface lane.

## Config requirements
Use the drawn form of `startpoint-line` for the visible start marker, the drawn form of `trigger-finish` for the distinct tenth ring, `volume-open` for the aerial play volume, and `hazard-kill` for the terrain below as an off-course crash surface. All exactly 10 floating ring meshes are required scene-specific geometry.

## Layout requirements
For `startpoint-line`, place one dragon StartPoint immediately before ring 1, aimed through it. Use `trigger-lap` for exactly nine ordered detection volumes aligned with rings 1 through 9. For `trigger-finish`, place exactly one terminal detection volume in ring 10. Number and activate all ten rings in strict sequence. Place one free-text BoundaryZone loss detector against the ground below the flight envelope.

## Layout components
The build contains one aerial start, exactly 10 floating rings, one continuous open-air route, one final ring gate, and a simple fantasy landscape below. Ring positions define the only required path; no physical lane walls or spectator structures are added. The composition exposes the full ordered chain without self-crossing ambiguity.

## Render order
Use `authored_plan`: procedurally generate the connected point-to-point ring sequence as the authoritative blueprint, then produce its top-down and isometric fantasy views.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by a ten-ring aerial course whose numbered rings must remain legible. The theme is simple high fantasy beneath a dragon-flight route. Use `P6` because the ring order and course connectivity must be valid by construction, plus `CHECK` for movement through an open 3D flight volume.
